answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable work bond before it may claim rewards. A registry checks that the bond is posted and slashes it when independently verified duplicate identities submit the same task or collude on claims; honest agents recover the bond after review. This does not prove one person per agent, but makes a Sybil swarm costly: the attacker must immobilize capital for every identity and risks losing it. A quill-marked marble may be ferrous, but none of those labels substitutes for the bond.
